- DESCRIPTION (paste verbatim): "A home-lab project has two AI agents passing work between browser tabs via an automated courier — ordinary consumer subscriptions, no enterprise stack. The courier failed in three instructive ways: a rejected insertion, a suspected payload-boundary violation, and stale shared state. Each failure produced the same design answer: fail closed. The result is a refusal set worth stealing — never overwrite a human draft, never blind-retry, never widen your own permissions — plus provenance headers and stop conditions you could write in Python before your coffee gets cold. Best receipt: the package arrived, but the courier's confirmation sensor didn't recognize the signature, so it stopped and said so. Learn to tell transport success from sensor failure, and your agent plumbing gets boring — in the good way. (The speaker is not a Python programmer. He'll open with that; the failures happen above the language line.)"

He helps a nonprofit move people from underserved communities into their first tech jobs, and he builds multi-model agent systems that are not allowed to lie about whether they worked."

- Opener B: "When my agents started failing, my first debugging tool was print. My second was LinkedIn."

Mark requests: ‘Please post balenaetcher? Primagen n15 post request from team on bus, select best 3 but post all. As it downloads what are your choices’.

Interpretation: original technical-rant jokes for Mark's delivery, Primeagen-adjacent subject/energy, not attributed to or represented as words from ThePrimeagen. Meraki authored all candidates below; Mark's real experience supplies the premise. Comedy, not technical findings. Official Etcher link: https://etcher.balena.io/ .

Context: EVOO EV-C-116-7BK reset trouble; UNetbootin-extracted installer on exFAT failed to launch; USB preparation suspected, exact root cause unproven. Dell Vostro3520 used for cross-test, followed by unexpected firmware update on reboot (trigger unproven). Current owner choice: new8GB stick, fresh Lubuntu ISO, direct Etcher flash. No successful boot/flash claimed by this post. Humorous causal lines must not become troubleshooting evidence.

ALL15 — preserve the whole round:
1. balenaEtcher sounds like a guy who makes artisanal USB sticks. Small batch. Locally sourced boot sectors.
2. Eight hours preparing a build station. At this point, the operating system is a subplot.
3. I bought a cheap laptop to build a tiny Linux. So far, the only thing getting smaller is my list of requirements.
4. Windows said, ‘This device will automatically restart.’ Apparently that was a statement of philosophy.
5. The download stopped at thirty percent. That’s not progress. That’s a residency.
6. Secure Boot kept Linux out, then locked me out of Windows. Finally: platform neutrality.
7. I asked the BIOS to remember one USB stick. It remembered every Windows installation except the one I wanted.
8. I moved the USB to the other side and the laptop updated its firmware. That port is a portal.
9. ‘Have you tried turning it off and on again?’ Yes. It has used the opportunity to become a different computer.
10. My USB stick contains two bootloaders, a kernel, and absolutely no intention of booting.
11. The Dell saw me struggling with another laptop and decided it needed attention too.
12. We’re doing Waiting for Godot, but the technical production is called Waiting for GRUB.
13. Our Future File System knows exactly how much space you need. Unfortunately, the future still needs FAT32.
14. We’re pre-revenue, pre-product, and apparently pre-boot.
15. Everybody wants to rewrite Linux in Rust. I would like to write Linux to a USB.

MERAKI PICKS: #15 strongest closer (ambition versus actual goal); #8 strongest specific incident line; #1 strongest Etcher-name opener. Suggested mini-set:1 ->8 ->15. Reserves: #6 security reversal; #14 founder callback. #4 is a quieter absurdist alternative. No other seat's votes claimed.
